profile.address: 6805, Truman Drive, Harwood, Cass County, North Dakota, 58042
profile.reading:
This facility is Polaris Forge 2, a data center campus Applied Digital is developing on more than 900 contracted acres near Harwood, in Cass County, North Dakota, just north of Fargo. Applied Digital broke ground on the campus in September 2025, describing it at announcement as a $3 billion development designed for 280 megawatts of capacity with room to scale well beyond that figure -- a target the company has since made concrete: Polaris Forge 2's full build-out potential is now described as a 1-gigawatt campus. Power is being supplied through Cass County Electric Cooperative, with additional support from Minnkota Power Cooperative, and the company has said the site should reach initial operation in 2026 and its first 200 megawatts of critical IT capacity by 2027.

In October 2025 Applied Digital announced a roughly 15-year, $5 billion lease at Polaris Forge 2 with an unnamed "U.S.-based, investment-grade hyperscaler," covering 200 megawatts of critical IT load delivered across two buildings, with that same tenant holding a first right of refusal on an additional 800 megawatts as the campus expands toward its full 1-gigawatt potential. Applied Digital has said the Polaris Forge 2 lease, combined with tenancy at its companion Polaris Forge 1 campus elsewhere in North Dakota, brings its total leased hyperscale capacity in the state to roughly 600 megawatts. The company projects more than 200 permanent full-time jobs at the site once operational, in addition to contractor employment during construction.

Applied Digital's core business has evolved from Bitcoin-mining infrastructure toward leasing large blocks of purpose-built data center capacity to AI and high-performance-computing tenants, and Polaris Forge 2 reflects that shift: it is being built and financed as wholesale AI/HPC data center space for a hyperscale customer, not as a company-operated compute or mining facility. As is standard for a large, single-tenant hyperscale lease still under construction, neither Applied Digital nor its hyperscaler tenant has published building-level specifications such as rack density, cooling architecture, or either building's individual footprint. What is public comes from Applied Digital's own investor disclosures and North Dakota state and utility statements -- the level of detail typically available for a facility that has broken ground but has not yet reached its contracted operating capacity, and which is a fair public description of a project still mid-construction rather than a finished, occupied building.

reading.body:
Polaris Forge 2 is a 900-acre AI data center campus in Harwood, North Dakota, operated by Applied Digital. The operator has not published IT power capacity for this site. No power specifications, rack density, or tenant information appear in the operator's available materials for this campus.

North Dakota has three mapped data center facilities total and no published megawatt figures from any operator on record. This campus therefore ranks first in the state by published capacity, a distinction that reflects the state's minimal published infrastructure disclosure rather than confirmed scale. The operator's investor materials describe large North Dakota developments with $4 billion in planned investment and multi-megawatt power leases, but the company has not attributed specific figures to the Harwood location.

Without published power capacity, expected cooling architecture, grid interconnection details, or timeline, the campus cannot be assessed against other AI compute sites. The 900-acre footprint and $3 billion development cost cited by industry directories suggest material scale, but this site's relevance to AI scaling depends on power capacity and delivery timelines not yet disclosed.
